column1: # *** TWO BRAYLEY QUESTIONS, PUT TO THE INDEX - 17 September 2026. ***
# Work-list rows 129 and 130, both opened when the 1851 and 1861 censuses at Lower Gunstone were read.
# *** One comes back a controlled silence. The other comes back refuted, which is the more useful of
# the two because it stops a wrong person being adopted. ***
question

*** ROW 129. What became of ISABELLA BRAILEY *** , born London (St Andrew) about 1841, daughter of John Brailey and Georgina Temple? *** Last seen aged 20, unmarried, a NEEDLE WOMAN, in her widowed mother's house at Lower Gunstone, Bideford, in 1861. ***
column2: *** Marriages, BRAILEY and BRAYLEY, Devon 1861-1890: none. *** *** Marriages, both spellings, ALL of England and Wales 1858-1895: none. *** *** Deaths, both spellings, all England and Wales 1861-1925: none. ***
column3: *** SHE VANISHES FROM THE ENGLISH CIVIL REGISTERS AFTER 1861, AND THE NULL IS CONTROLLED. *** The control: *** BRAYLEY marriages with no forename, 1870 alone, returns FOURTEEN nationally *** - so the surname is thickly indexed and the searches were capable of finding her. *** She did not marry in England and she did not die in England under either spelling. *** The readings that fit: she EMIGRATED; or she married or died under one of the manglings this surname is notorious for. *** Nothing here decides between them. ***

column1: *** ROW 130. Is GEORGINA BRAYLEY, born London Kilburn about 1871 *** - a general servant in a draper's house at Tower Street, Northam, in 1891 - *** a daughter of JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY? ***
column2: *** Marriages, BRAYLEY, forename "John Walker", 1863-1880, all counties. ***
column3: *** REFUTED, and cleanly. *** *** JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY MARRIED IN THE DECEMBER QUARTER OF 1876, AT BIDEFORD - 5b/978. *** That is *** FIVE YEARS AFTER *** a child born at Kilburn in 1871. *** She cannot be his daughter by that marriage ***, and the pattern this archive was reasoning from - a Brayley of the right age, in service at Northam, carrying the family's forename - *** was a resemblance and nothing more. She is not adopted. ***

column1: # *** AND THE SEARCH THAT REFUTED ONE THING SUPPLIED ANOTHER. ***
# Page *** 5b/978, Bideford, December quarter 1876 *** carries four names: *** BONNING Elizabeth,
# BRAYLEY John Walker, PADDON Elizabeth, RICHARDS John. *** Two marriages on one page.
# *** So JOHN WALKER BRAYLEY MARRIED AN ELIZABETH - either BONNING or PADDON - and the index cannot say
# which, exactly as it could not for his sister's marriage on 5b/794 six years earlier. *** The
# certificate would settle it and would name his father.
# *** ONE THING WORTH SAYING ABOUT ISABELLA, CAREFULLY. ***
# *** Sue Rowbotham's family history has a chapter called "The mystery of the missing husband and
# daughter". *** The missing husband is now firmly JOHN BRAILEY - alive in the county asylum on census
# night 1851 and dead there five weeks later.
# *** Of the four children of John Brailey and Georgina Temple, THREE have documented later lives: ***
# Mary Ann Hellen married in 1870 and died in 1900; John Walker married in 1876 and died in 1900;
# Georgina Margaret lived to about 1940. *** ISABELLA ALONE HAS NOTHING AFTER 1861. ***
# *** THAT MAKES HER THE BEST CANDIDATE FOR THE MISSING DAUGHTER, AND IT IS STILL NOT EVIDENCE. *** It
# is an argument from what is absent, which is the weakest kind there is, and it is recorded as a
# candidate so that somebody can test it against Sue Rowbotham's own text rather than against a guess.
# ================= ROW 128: THE TENTH TAYLOR CHILD - AND WHY FREEBMD CANNOT ANSWER IT =================
# *** The count argument, restated so it is checkable. *** "SEPTIMA" MEANS SEVENTH. The daughters of
# William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley, as the birth index gives them, are *** Kathleen Georgina
# (1870), Isabella Temple (1874), Margaret Hellen Walker (1876), Irene (1879), Lucy Elizabeth (1881) ***
# - and then Mary Septima (Dec quarter 1884). *** That makes her the SIXTH. For her name to mean what it
# says, ONE DAUGHTER IS MISSING, BORN BEFORE DECEMBER 1884. ***
# *** THE SEARCH THIS ROW WAS OPENED TO RUN, NOW RUN: infant deaths. *** The reasoning was that a child
# who died before 1891 would sit in the birth index, be counted among the family's ten, and appear in no
# census - which is exactly the shape of the person missing.
# *** FreeBMD deaths, TAYLOR, BIDEFORD district, 1881-1891: 37 entries, of which FOURTEEN are aged 0-3. ***
candidate
*** ETHEL Taylor ***
column4: *** FITS THE GAP EXACTLY *** - born between Lucy Elizabeth (Sep 1881) and Mary Septima (Dec 1884), and dead before any census could record her. *** AND SHE CANNOT BE ATTACHED TO THIS FAMILY. ***

column1: # *** SO THE HONEST VERDICT ON ROW 128: FREEBMD CANNOT SETTLE IT, AND NO AMOUNT OF FURTHER SEARCHING
# THERE WILL. *** The reason is structural and worth writing down once:
# *** THE FREEBMD BIRTH INDEX CARRIES NO MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME, AND THE DEATH INDEX CARRIES NO PARENTS. ***
# There is therefore *** no field anywhere in FreeBMD that can join a Bideford Taylor child to THIS
# Taylor household ***, and every candidate above is a name in the right town in the right year and
# nothing more. *** This archive has been wrong before by promoting exactly that. ***
# *** WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT IN ONE SEARCH, AND IT IS DAVID'S TO RUN. ***
# *** THE GRO'S OWN ONLINE INDEX AT gro.gov.uk IS NOT FREEBMD, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT:
# IT GIVES THE MOTHER'S MAIDEN NAME ON EVERY BIRTH FROM 1837. *** FreeBMD does not and never will.
# *** THE SEARCH: births, surname TAYLOR, mother's maiden name BRAYLEY, district BIDEFORD, 1870-1890. ***
# *** That returns EVERY child of William Taylor and Mary Ann Hellen Brayley, by definition, with no
# inference required - the tenth child included, whoever she was. *** It needs a free GRO account, and
# this session does not create accounts.
